questions.stem: In Zellweger syndrome, which of the following is absent?
questions.solutionHtml:
Peroxisomes

Zellweger syndrome is a rare disease characterized by the absence of functional peroxisomes.

  • The long chain fatty acids (C26-C36) are not oxidized. They accumulate in tissues, particularly in brain, liver and kidney. Hence the disorder is also known as cerebrohepatorenal syndrome.
  • This condition is apparent at birth and is characterized by profound neurologic impairment, victims often dying within a year.
  • Two closely related conditions are neonatal adrenoleukodystrophy and infantile Refsum disease. Zellweger syndrome and these two conditions represent a spectrum of overlapping features, with Zellweger syndrome being the most severe (many proteins affected) and infantile Refsum disease the least severe

questions.stem: Creatinine, No & urea are synthesized from which amino acid?
questions.solutionHtml:
Arginine

Creatinine – Three amino acid -glycine, arginine and methionine-are required for creatine formation

  • Creatine is reversibly phosphorylated to phosphocreatine (creatine phosphate) by creatine kinase. lt is stored in muscle as high energy phosphate.
  • NO – ARGININE
  • UREA – Arginine is the immediate precursor for urea.
  • Arginase is the fifth and final enzyme that cleaves arginine to yield urea and ornithine
  • Arginase enzyme is mostly found in liver but the other urea cycle enzyme found in other tissue also
  • For this reason, arginine synthesis may occur to varying degrees in many tissues. But only the liver can ultimately produce urea

questions.stem: Which of the following is not the source of cytosolic NADPH:-
questions.solutionHtml:
ATP citrate lyase

SOURCE of NADPH – (1)   HMP PATHWAY – main enzyme is G6PD

  • This is an alternative pathway to glycolysis and TCA cycle for the oxidation of glucose
  • It is concerned with the biosynthesis of NADPH and pentoses.
  • Malic enzyme - Malic enzyme converts malate to pyruvate. NADPH and CO2 are generated in this reaction. Both of them are utilized for fatty acid synthesis.
  • Cytosolic isocitrate dehydrogenase - There are three isoenzymes of isocitrate dehydrogenase. One, which uses nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+), is found only in mitochondria. The other two use NADP+ and are found in mitochondria and the cytosol. Respiratory chain– linked oxidation of isocitrate occurs through the NAD+-dependent enzyme.

Use of NADPH –

  • Biosynthesis of fatty acids and steroid.
  • NADPH is responsible for the regeneration of reduced glutathione from the oxidized form.
  • NADPH maintains the concentration of reduced glutathione which is essentially required to preserve the integrity of RBC membrane

questions.stem: True regarding mitochondrial DNA is:

options.label: D
options.text: All respiratory proteins are synthesized within mitochondria itself

questions.solutionHtml:
Inherited from mother

The mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) has structural and functional resemblances with prokaryotic DNA

  • mtDNA is circular in nature and contains about 16,000 nucleotide bases
  • A vast majority of structural and functional proteins of the mitochondria are synthesized in the cvtosol under the influence of nuclear DNA. However, certain proteins (around 13), most of them being the components of electron transport chain, are synthesized in the mitochondria (e.g. cytochrome b of complex lll, two subunits of ATP synthase.
  • mtDNA is inherited from the mother
  • Mitochondrial DNA is subjected to high rate of mutations (about 10 times more than nuclear DNA)
  • Diseases related to mitochondrial DNA
  • MELAS (mitochondrial encephalopathy lactic acidosis stroke like episode)
  • Leber hereditary optic neuropathy
  • Leigh syndrome
  • Kearns sayre syndrome
  • NARP syndrome

questions.stem: Vitamin A is stored in:-
questions.solutionHtml:
Ito cells

Vitamin A –

  • The fat soluble vitamin A, as such is present only in foods of animal origin. However, its provitamins carotenes are found in plants
  • Retinol, retinal and retinoic acid are regarded as vitamers of vitamin A.
  • The stored in ito cell in the liver.
  • Ito cell – also know as hepatic stellate cell , vit A storing cell ,lipocytes ,perisinusoidal cell
  • They are present between parenchymal cell and liver sinusoidal endothelial cell that why they know as perisinusoidal cell
  • They store 50 -80 % vit A in the whole body as retinyl palmitate
  • Function of vit A - Vitamin A is necessary for a variety of functions such as vision, proper growth and differentiation, reproduction and maintenance of epithelial cells.
  • Deficiency manifestations of the eyes – nyctalopia is one of the earliest symptoms of vitamin A deficiency.

CLINICAL FEATURES

  • WHO CLASSIFICATION:
  • XN             NIGHT BLINDNESS
  • XIA            CONJUCTIVAL XEROSIS
  • XIB             BITOT'S SPOTS
  • X2             CORNEAL XEROSIS
  • X3A            COR. ULCER <1/3 OF COR. SURFACE
  • X3B            COR. ULCER >1/3 OF COR. SURFACE
  • XS             COR. SCAR
  • XF             XEROPHTHALMIC FUNDUS
  • Effect on reproduction: The reproduction system is adversely affected in vitamin A deficiency. Degeneration of germinal epithelium leads to sterility in males.
  • Effect on skin and epithelial cells: The skin becomes rough and dry. Keratinization of epithelial cells of gastrointestinal tract, urinary tract and respiratory tract is noticed. This leads to increased bacterial infection.
  • Vitamin A deficiency is associated with formation of urinary stones

questions.stem: In Wilson disease there is less urinary excretion of:-
questions.solutionHtml:
Methyl-Histidine

Wilson disease –

  • A mutation in the gene for a copper-binding P-type ATPase (ATP7B protein) blocks the excretion of excess copper in the bile
  • copper accumulates in liver,  brain ,kidney ,RBC
  • Rising levels of copper within the liver apparently interferes with the incorporation of this metal into newly synthesized ceruloplasmin polypeptides  leading to a fall in plasma ceruloplasmin levels
  • Patient develop hemolytic anemia and liver disease
  • Accumulation of copper in basal ganglia lead to neurological symptoms
  • Urinary levels of 3-methylhistidine are unusually low in patients with Wilson disease (Harpers Illustrated Biochemistry 31th Edition PG NO -732)
  • Treated by limiting the dietary intake of copper while depleting any excess copper by the regular administration of penicillamine, which chelates copper and is subsequently excreted in the urine

questions.stem: A 20 year old alcoholic malnourished patient presented to hospital with respiratory distress. His pulse was 112/minute. Patient had edema, hypertension, systolic murmur along the left sternal edge. Bilateral murmur along the left sternal edge. Bilateral crepitations were felt in the lungs. A diagnosis of congetsive high output cardiac failure was made. Which vitamin is deficient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Vitamin B1

Vitamin B 1 – water soluble vitamin

  • It has a specific coenzyme TPP (thiamine pyrophosphate ) this help in carbohydrate metabolism .
  • TPP Dependent enzyme
    • Pyruvate dehydrogenase - conversion of pyruvate to acetyl CoA.
    • Alpha -Ketoglutarate dehydrogenase – CTA CYCLE
    • Transketolas - (HMP shunt)
    • The branched chain ALPHA - keto acid dehydrogenase -: oxidative decarboxylation pyrophosphate of branched chain amino acids .
  • RDA ( Recommended dietary allowance)
  • Adult –   1 – 1.5 mg/day
  • Children – 0.7 – 1.2 mg /day
  • The requirement increases in pregnancy and lactation (2 mg/ day), old age and alcoholism.
  • Deficiency of vitamin b 1 is known as beriberi
  • In adults, two types of beri-beri

WET BERI – BERI - This is characterized by edema of legs, face, trunk and serous cavities.

  • Dyspnea and palpitation are present
  • The systolic blood pressure is elevated while diastolic is decreased
  • Pulse is fast and bouncing
  • Death is due to heart failure

Dry beri-beri - This is associated with neurological manifestations resulting in peripheral neuritis.

  • Edema is not seen
  • Muscle become week so patient has difficulty in walking.

Infantile beri-beri - infant born to mother who is suffering from thiamine deficiency

  • Brest milk is contain low thiamine
  • Sleeplessness , vomiting , convulsions
  • Bouts of screaming – resembles to abdominal colic
  • These all symptoms are due cardiac dilation
  • Death occur suddenly due to heart failure

Wernickes Korsakoff syndrome

  • Seen in chronic alcoholics
  • insufficient intake or impaired intestinal absorption of thiamine will lead to this syndrome
  • Symptoms of wernickes encephalopathy -
  • G – GLOBAL CONFUSION
  • O – OPHTHALMOPLEGIA
  • A – ATAXIA
  • Korsakoff syndrome – chronic neurological complication
    • Amnesia - mainly anterograde amnesia
    • Confabulations – false story and honest lying
  • Thiamin Nutritional Status Can Be Assessed by Erythrocyte Transketolase Activaity

questions.stem: Amino acid linking Kreb's cycle & urea cycle:-
questions.solutionHtml:
Aspartate

Urea cycle and TCA Cycle is linked by three way

  • fumarate in urea cycle is the most important integrating point with TCA cycle.
  • Fumarate is converted to malate and then to oxaloacetate in TCA cycle. Oxaloacetate undergoes transamination to produce aspartate which enters urea cycle
  • Fumarate is not a amino acid so amino acid linking krebs cycle and urea cycle is aspartate
  • 12 ATP are generated in the TCA cycle while 4 ATP are utilized for UREA CYCLE
  • The CO2liberated in TCA cycle (in the mitochondria) can be utilized in urea cycle

questions.stem: Retinitis pigmentosa patients don’t have:-
questions.solutionHtml:

  • Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA; ω3, 22:6), which is synthesized to a limited extent from α-linolenic acid or obtained directly from fish oils, is present in high concentrations in retina, cerebral cortex, testis, and sperm. questions.stem: Which apolipoprotein is responsible for Alzheimer’s disease:-
questions.solutionHtml:
APOE4

questions.stem: Which amino acid is used to synthesis Nitric oxide?
questions.solutionHtml:
Arginine

Nitric oxide (NO) –

  • Arginine is the substrate for the production of nitric oxide (NO)
  • ENZYME - nitric oxide synthase
  • Half life – about 5 sec.

Functions –

  • Vasodilator and relaxation of smooth muscles
  • Regulation of blood flow and BP
  • Inhibitor of platelet aggregation
  • Neurotransmitter
  • NO mediates the bactericidal actions of macrophages
  • Erection of peni
  • Nitric oxide promotes the synthesis of cGMP.

 

Glycine –

  • Formation of purine ring
  • Synthesis of glutathione
  • Conjugation reactions – two reactions
    • A - The bile acids-cholic acid and chenodeoxy cholic acid-are conjugated with glycine
    • B - glycine is important for detoxification of benzoic acid
  • Heme synthesis
  • Biosynthesis of creatine

Histidine - generation of histamine

  • This amino acid is oxidatively deaminated by histidase to urocanic acid, which subsequently forms N-formiminoglutamate ([FIGlu]
  • Individuals deficient in folic acid excrete increased amounts of FIGlu in the urine, particularly after ingestion of a large dose of histidine. The FIGlu excretion test has been used in diagnosing a deficiency of folic acid.

Tyrosine - Tyrosine is formed from phenylalanine by phenylalanine hydroxylase

  •  Biosynthesis of thyroid hormones ,catecholamines ,melanin

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a Ribozyme?
questions.solutionHtml:
Transpeptidase

RIBOZYME - Ribozymes are RNA molecules with catalytic activity

  • At least five distinct species of RNA that act as catalysts have been identified. Three are involved in the self processing reactions of RNAs while the other two are regarded as true catalysts (RNase P and rRNA).

(1)R RNA-   23S RNA (prokaryotes)

  • 28s RNA (eukaryotes)
  • Peptidyl transferase / transpeptidase - catalyzes peptide bond formation on the ribosome

(2) splicing –  After transcription, during RNA processing, introns are removed and the exons are ligated together to form the mature mRNA that appears in the cytoplasm; this process is termed RNA

  • splicing
  • Ribozyme Sn RNA having role in removal in introns . 

(3) RIBONUCLEASE P - It cleaves t RNA precursors to generate mature tRNA molecules.
